necessary_mathematical_assumptions: SourceProper globally excludes bottom and supplies a finite witness; effectiveDomain alone only excludes top.
Literal V convex and contained in effectiveDomain; lambda nonnegative; exact interior interpolation with lambda/2.
p and q belong to literal V; selected real continuous linear functional globally defined; its affine support inequality holds at every z in V.
No support existence, minimizer existence, nonzero g, closedness, completeness, finite dimension, or positive modulus is asserted.
source_delta: Lemma4.2 literally assumes V subset dom(partial f), not merely dom f. Its forward direction at a selected support needs only support at p; the candidate explicitly drops support existence at all other V points and localizes support to V. This is a valid generalized forward implication, not the full printed iff.

Finite-dimensional coordinate dot-product support becomes an element of the continuous real dual on an arbitrary real normed space. Continuity is stronger than algebraic necessity for this inequality, but appropriate for future dual-norm estimates; it must remain an explicit interface generalization.
Source proof uses the segment and alpha-to-zero limit. Affine tilt plus existing minimum-growth is an alternative mathematical dependency route, not the literal proof topology.
